pr_title: Fixed #34752 -- Fixed handling ASGI http.disconnect for streaming responses.
pr_body:
See this ticket for details: https://code.djangoproject.com/ticket/34752

This PR:

- [x] Adds some tests to ensures that ASGI `http.disconnect` is handled correctly during `StreamingHttpResponses`.
- [x] Modifies the existing ASGI handler so that the test passes.
- [x] Updates the `StreamingHttpResponse` documentation to document this new feature.

Additional context from a comment I made on the ticket:

> One subtlety: I originally made a smaller modification to the handler that put view logic and response logic in the same coroutine, but otherwise  followed the same flow. I found this broke in practice because sometimes  //both// coroutines would return at once. This caused the previous  `pending.pop()`/`done.pop()` logic to error out because one of those two  sets would be empty. I think that this problem is particularly likely to  happen in situations where some coroutines are long-lived. I haven't added  a test for this edge case yet, though.

gold_defects.description: Comment notes the bug only manifests in production (Daphne) not in existing unit tests, and author commits to writing a test later.
gold_defects.original_comment_excerpt:
Assuming you mean the change from

```
done, pending = await asyncio.wait(tasks, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
done, pending = done.pop(), pending.pop()
# some conditionals to handle done and pending
```

to

```
await asyncio.wait(tasks, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
# a loop through tasks
```

The answer is that both tasks can finish at the same time, which means that both tasks end up in `done` and the `pending.pop()` errors out. I only observed this behavior when

pr_title: Fixed #33738 -- Allowed handling ASGI http.disconnects in long-lived requests.
pr_body:
To fix [#33738](https://code.djangoproject.com/ticket/33738). 

We were not handling the ASGI http.disconnect message correctly. Since it's only dealt with whilst reading the request body, http.disconnect is not processed on a request that includes a body.

If a user sends a disconnect while an initial request was yet to receive a response, it will be best to wait for a possible disconnect (just for a few seconds) before returning a response.

Using asyncio.wait_for we can listen for a possible disconnect for 0.05 seconds before sending a response to the client.

gold_defects.description: Comment text "raise request aborted if http.disconnect was received" has grammatical error ("raise request" should be "raise an exception" or similar); pure wording/clarity issue in a docstring.
gold_defects.original_comment_excerpt: raise request aborted if http.disconnect was received.

gold_defects.description: Reviewer points out that adding a pause for the uncommon disconnect case adds significant latency to the hot path, suggesting get_nowait() as a better alternative.
gold_defects.original_comment_excerpt:
I don't think pausing here is the way forward. The happy path is no disconnect, and we're adding a quite big delay to check for the deviant case. 

We should be able to use [get_nowait](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/asyncio-queue.html#asyncio.Queue.get_nowait) in this context no? 🤔

(But see overview comment: I'm not sure this is the right approach.)

gold_defects.description: Comment identifies that RequestAborted exception is raised but TimeoutError is never raised despite no response being sent, indicating incomplete error handling.
gold_defects.original_comment_excerpt: @carltongibson This exception is raised and the function returns None but TimeoutError is not raised to pass the test. The send_response task is pending when the RequestAborted exception is raised but the Timeout Error is never raised even though no response is sent to the client.

gold_defects.description: Reviewer points out logic error: view is still running synchronously instead of being wrapped in concurrent task to handle disconnects during long-lived requests.
gold_defects.original_comment_excerpt:
Hey @Th3nn3ss — This isn't quite what I'm suggesting. Here you're still running the view, and only checking the disconnect before sending it. 

Rather if you wrap everything from ≈ln172 in to just before the `send_response` call in a `get_response()` or `run_view()` method, then you can run **that** concurrently to the `listen_for_disconnect` task. 

At first glance, I think if we get a disconnect between view finishing and the response being sent, we can just ignore that.

gold_defects.description: Comment identifies a race condition where asyncio.wait ordering causes listen_for_disconnect to not run first, requiring forced await sleep to fix task execution order.
gold_defects.original_comment_excerpt: asyncio.wait is inconsistent with the task it runs first. forcing signal_to_start_request to await sleep allows listen_for_disconnect to run first (at least once).

gold_defects.description: Reviewer suggests unnecessary loop contradicts ASGI spec which allows only one http.disconnect event after body processing, risking incorrect behavior.
gold_defects.original_comment_excerpt:
I'm not sure we need the loop here. 🤔 The spec doesn't allow any `receive` events except `http.disconnect` once the body processing is completed. 

So we should get at most one event, and we can `assert message["type"] == "http.disconnect"` for that event, erroring loudly for anything else.

gold_defects.description: Comment requests a test for view cleanup on client disconnect, identifying missing test coverage for the feature being implemented.
gold_defects.original_comment_excerpt:
Does the `pending` task needs to be cancelled? 

There should be a test for a view cleaning up after itself. (This will feed into docs for this... — _"If you have a long running request, you may need to clean up in case the client disconnects before you're finished..."_)

gold_defects.description: Comment suggests test needs refactoring to properly send disconnect before view finishes, indicating current test structure cannot adequately verify the fix's behavior.
gold_defects.original_comment_excerpt: Create a view function that has this delay in it, rather than in the test, so that we can send the disconnect before the view finishes. See the `urls.py` sibling to this file.

pr_title: Use `classmethod` instead of `classmethod[Any, Any, Any]`

## Change Summary

Using `classmethod` is equivalent to `classmethod[Any, Any, Any]` and was recommended in [this](https://github.com/python/typeshed/pull/9771#issuecomment-1469835536) comment. This change fixes an issue discussed [here](https://github.com/tox-dev/sphinx-autodoc-typehints/issues/375#issuecomment-1706579147). There is no expectation that code within `if TYPE_CHECKING` blocks is always executable, but this seems like a quick win with no downsides.

gold_defects.description: Comment suggests renaming variable from `Validator` to `Adapter` in docs to better convey TypeAdapter's broader capabilities beyond validation.
gold_defects.original_comment_excerpt:
```suggestion
UserListAdapter = TypeAdapter(List[User])
```
(and below).

I think better to use `Adapter` than `Validator` to help people realize it's able to do more than validation, also I just think it's a better naming convention and would want to push people toward using it as they read the docs, even if they are only doing validation with the value.

    When creating an instance of `TypeAdapter`, the provided type must be analyzed and converted into a pydantic-core
    schema. This comes with some non-trivial overhead, so it is recommended to create a `TypeAdapter` for a given type
    just once and reuse it in loops or other performance-critical code.
```

pr_title: Don't decode bytes (which may not be UTF8) when displaying SecretBytes
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

Removes unneeded `.decode()`.

I couldn't find any justification for decoding the bytes. The code was introduced in [this commit](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/5674/commits/b904b986b6ef7d7fd8b59caf55ade9ae48945d94#diff-f7a381c0918da7ec905bfbe6aff2ccc72c2d0fd6da0dd3011ef1da892e42d57aR497-R498) in https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/5674 and I don't see any PR comments explaining it. @adriangb any idea?

There are some encodings where a non-empty byte string can decode to any empty string:

```python
>>> ''.encode('utf16')
b'\xff\xfe'
>>> ''.encode('utf16').decode('utf16')
''
>>> ''.encode('utf16').decode('utf16') == ''
True
```

but `.decode()` without arguments should always use UTF8 in Python 3 regardless of locale settings.

I've checked that any non-empty byte string with up to 3 bytes decodes to a non-empty string if it can be decoded at all:

```python
import itertools

count = 0
total = 0
for length in [1, 2, 3]:
    for b in itertools.product(range(256), repeat=length):
        total += 1
        b = bytes(b)
        assert b
        assert len(b) == length > 0
        try:
            s = b.decode()
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            continue
        assert s
        assert len(s) > 0
        assert b == s.encode()
        count += 1

print(count)  # 2668544
print(total)  # 16843008
```

I also think that any non-empty byte string should be treated as non-empty when displaying even if it can be decoded to an empty unicode string. Although I'm also not sure about revealing whether *any* secret value is empty.

## Related issue number

Closes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/7971
